verses.zh: 主耶和华如此说：「内院朝东的门，在办理事务的六日内必须关闭；惟有安息日和月朔必须敞开。
verses.en: “‘This is what the Sovereign Lord says: The gate of the inner court that faces east[NOTE:1] will be closed six working days, but on the Sabbath day it will be opened and on the day of the new moon it will be opened.
notes: The east gate of the outer court was permanently closed (Ezek 44:2).
verses.commentary:
46:1 "the gate of the inner court facing east" Remember the outer eastern gate was permanently sealed (cf.
Ezek. 44:2) because this is the gate by which YHWH left the temple (cf. Ezekiel 10) and returned (cf. Ezekiel 43).

▣ "the new moon" This monthly feast is first mentioned in Num. 10:10 and explained in Num. 28:11-15.
It is referred to in Ps. 81:3-5 and Ezek. 45:18; 46:3,6. Since the tabernacle was set up on the first day
of the month (cf. Exod. 40:2,17), it is possible that it is connected to this event.

The Jews used a lunar calendar.

Special Topic: ANE Calendars

verses.zh: 王要从这门的廊进入，站在门框旁边。祭司要为他预备燔祭和平安祭，他就要在门槛那里敬拜，然后出去。这门直到晚上不可关闭。
verses.en: The prince will enter by way of the porch of the gate from the outside and will stand by the doorpost of the gate. The priests will provide his burnt offering and his peace offerings, and he will bow down at the threshold of the gate and then go out. But the gate will not be closed until evening.
verses.commentary:
46:2 "his burnt offerings and his peace offerings" Also note, verse 12 lists several other offerings.

Special Topic: Burnt Offering

Special Topic: Peace Offering

Special Topic: Sacrificial Systems of the Ancient Near East

▣ "he shall worship" This is an unusual form of a common religious concept of "worship" or
"bow down" (BDB 1005, KB 295 II, Histaphel PERFECT
with waw).

The basic stem seems to be חוה (KB 295 II), which in Ugaritic means
"to prostrate oneself in worship" or שחה, "to bow down" (BDB 1005). It occurs three
times in this paragraph (cf. Ezek. 46:2,3,9).

The prince has a special place at the gateway of the inner court where he can see the
sacrificing being made, but cannot enter the sacred precincts of the priests.

Special Topic: Worship

▣ "the gate shall not be shut" This is imagery of access and availability (cf. Isa. 60:11; Rev. 21:25). YHWH
would receive the prince and the people in regular worship at all times.

▣ "the prince" This future Davidic leader ("prince," BDB 672) is mentioned several times in Ezekiel.

- YHWH will establish him as shepherd over a united covenant people, Ezek. 34:20-24

- YHWH will restore the covenant people to their land and restore their Davidic prince. He will make an
everlasting covenant of peace with an obedient Israel, Ezek. 37:24-28

- he will eat/worship before YHWH in the new temple, Ezek. 44:2-3; 46:1-12

- he shall receive a large special land allotment (i.e. great wealth) on both sides of the temple area to
keep him from oppressing the people, Ezek. 45:7-8; 48:21-22

- the people will give offerings to the prince so that he can provide sacrifices on special days,
Ezek. 45:13-25

- regulations about inheritance gifts given by the prince, Ezek. 46:16-18

verses.zh: 在安息日和月朔，国内的居民要在这门口，耶和华面前敬拜。
verses.en: The people of the land will bow down at the entrance of that gate before the Lord on the Sabbaths and on the new moons.

verses.zh: 安息日，王所献与耶和华的燔祭要用无残疾的羊羔六只，无残疾的公绵羊一只；
verses.en: The burnt offering that the prince will offer to the Lord on the Sabbath day will be six unblemished lambs and one unblemished ram.
verses.commentary:
46:4-7 The prince shall offer

- the sabbath

- six lambs

- one ram

- one ephah of grain (with ram)

- as much as able of grain (with the lambs)

- a hin of oil

- new moon

- a young bull

- six lambs

- a ram

- one ephah of grain (with bull)

- one ephah of grain (with ram)

- as much as able of grain (with lambs)

- a hin of oil

46:4 "without blemish" This term (BDB 1071) denotes an animal that is healthy and without obvious defect.
In other words, it is a prime example (typical) of its breed in color, shape, and size (i.e. Exod. 12:5;
Lev. 3:1).

Special Topic: Blameless, Innocent, Guiltless, Without Reproach

verses.zh: 同献的素祭要为公绵羊献一伊法细面，为羊羔照他的力量而献，一伊法细面加油一欣。
verses.en: The grain offering will be an ephah with the ram, and the grain offering with the lambs will be as much as he is able to give,[NOTE:1] and a gallon[NOTE:2] of olive oil with an ephah.
notes: Or “as much as he wishes.” Heb “a gift of his hand.”
Heb “a hin of oil.” A hin was about 1/16 of a bath. See L. C. Allen, Ezekiel (WBC), 2:266, and O. R. Sellers, “Weights,” IDB 4:835 g.
verses.commentary: 46:5 "ephah. . .hin" See Special Topic: ANE Weights and Volumes (metrology).

verses.zh: 当月朔，要献无残疾的公牛犊一只，羊羔六只，公绵羊一只，都要无残疾的。
verses.en: On the day of the new moon he will offer[NOTE:1] an unblemished young bull and six lambs and a ram, all without blemish.
notes: The phrase “he will offer” is not in the Hebrew text but is warranted from the context.

verses.zh: 他也要预备素祭，为公牛献一伊法细面，为公绵羊献一伊法细面，为羊羔照他的力量而献，一伊法细面加油一欣。
verses.en: He will provide a grain offering: an ephah with the bull and an ephah with the ram, and with the lambs as much as he wishes,[NOTE:1] and a gallon[NOTE:2] of olive oil with each ephah of grain.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “with the lambs as his hand can reach.”
Heb “a hin of oil.” A hin was about 1/16 of a bath. See L. C. Allen, Ezekiel (WBC), 2:266, and O. R. Sellers, “Weights,” IDB 4:835 g.
Heb “ephah.” The words “of grain” are supplied in the translation as a clarification.
verses.commentary:
46:7

NASB
"as much as he is able"

NKJV, TEV
"as much as he wants to give"

NRSV
"as much as he wishes"

NJB
"what he pleases"

LXX
"according as his hand can furnish"

Peshitta, JPSOA, REB
"as much as he can afford"

The literal phrase is "as much as his hand can reach." The amount of sacrifices depended on
two things.

- the free-will offerings of the people

- the wealth and/or ability and/or desire of the monarch

verses.zh: 王进入的时候必由这门的廊而入，也必由此而出。
verses.en: When the prince enters, he will come by way of the porch of the gate and will go out the same way.

verses.zh: 在各节期，国内居民朝见耶和华的时候，从北门进入敬拜的，必由南门而出；从南门进入的，必由北门而出。不可从所入的门而出，必要直往前行，由对门而出。
verses.en: “‘When the people of the land come before the Lord at the appointed feasts, whoever enters by way of the north gate to worship will go out by way of the south gate; whoever enters by way of the south gate will go out by way of the north gate. No one will return by way of the gate they entered but will go out straight ahead.
verses.commentary:
46:9 There were great crowds of people at the temple during the feast days. The procedure of verse 9
was to help with the congestion.

verses.zh: 民进入，王也要在民中进入；民出去，王也要一同出去。
verses.en: When they come in, the prince will come in with them, and when they go out, he will go out.
verses.commentary:
46:10 The prince has a special place to observe the sacrifices on the "special" days (i.e. appointed feasts),
but on other days he was not allowed even this special place, but must enter and exit with other covenant people.

verses.zh: 「在节期和圣会的日子同献的素祭，要为一只公牛献一伊法细面，为一只公绵羊献一伊法细面，为羊羔照他的力量而献，一伊法细面加油一欣。
verses.en: “‘At the festivals and at the appointed feasts the grain offering will be an ephah with the bull and an ephah with the ram, and with the lambs as much as one is able,[NOTE:1] and a gallon[NOTE:2] of olive oil with each ephah of grain.[NOTE:3]
notes: Or “as much as he wishes.” Heb “a gift of his hand.”
Heb “a hin of oil.” A hin was about 1/16 of a bath. See L. C. Allen, Ezekiel (WBC), 2:266, and O. R. Sellers, “Weights,” IDB 4:835 g.
Heb “ephah.” The words “of grain” are supplied in the translation as a clarification.

verses.zh: 王预备甘心献的燔祭或平安祭，就是向耶和华甘心献的，当有人为他开朝东的门。他就预备燔祭和平安祭，与安息日预备的一样，献毕就出去。他出去之后，当有人将门关闭。」
verses.en: When the prince provides a freewill offering, a burnt offering, or peace offerings as a voluntary offering to the Lord, the gate facing east will be opened for him, and he will provide his burnt offering and his peace offerings just as he did on the Sabbath. Then he will go out, and the gate will be closed after he goes out.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “he shall shut the gate after he goes out.”

verses.zh: 「每日，你要预备无残疾一岁的羊羔一只，献与耶和华为燔祭；要每早晨预备。
verses.en: “‘You[NOTE:1] will provide a lamb a year old without blemish for a burnt offering daily to the Lord; morning by morning he will provide it.
notes: A few Hebrew mss, the LXX, and the Vulgate read the verb as third person singular (referring to the prince), both here and later in the verse.
verses.commentary:
46:13

NASB, NKJV, REB
"you"

NRSV, NJB, LXX, Peshitta, Vulgate
"he"

The MT has "you," but ancient translations (and some Hebrew MSS) understood it as a reference
to "the prince" (same in Ezek. 46:14).

▣ "morning by morning" This refers to the "continual" (i.e. post-exilic designation), which was a lamb offered
every morning and evening at the temple (cf. Exod. 29:38-42; Num. 28:3-4; 2 Kgs. 16:15). This continued in the time of Jesus.

verses.zh: 每早晨也要预备同献的素祭，细面一伊法六分之一，并油一欣三分之一，调和细面。这素祭要常献与耶和华为永远的定例。
verses.en: And you[NOTE:1] will provide a grain offering with it morning by morning, a sixth of an ephah and a third of a gallon[NOTE:2] of olive oil to moisten the choice flour, as a grain offering to the Lord; this is a perpetual statute.
notes: Two medieval Hebrew mss, the LXX, the Syriac, and the Vulgate read the verb as third person singular.
Heb “a hin of oil.” A hin was about 1/16 of a bath. See L. C. Allen, Ezekiel (WBC), 2:266, and O. R. Sellers, “Weights,” IDB 4:835 g.
verses.commentary:
46:14 "a perpetual ordinance" The Hebrew term "forever" (עולמ, BDB 761) is used
in several senses as the Special Topic shows and must be interpreted in each context.

Special Topic: Forever ('olam and aiōnios)

verses.zh: 每早晨要这样预备羊羔、素祭，并油为常献的燔祭。」
verses.en: Thus they will provide the lamb, the grain offering, and the olive oil morning by morning as a perpetual burnt offering.

verses.zh: 主耶和华如此说：「王若将产业赐给他的儿子，就成了他儿子的产业，那是他们承受为业的。
verses.en: “‘This is what the Sovereign Lord says: If the prince should give a gift to one of his sons as[NOTE:1] his inheritance, it will belong to his sons; it is their property by inheritance.
notes: The Hebrew text has no preposition; the LXX reads “from” (see v. 17).

verses.zh: 倘若王将一分产业赐给他的臣仆，就成了他臣仆的产业；到自由之年仍要归与王。至于王的产业，必归与他的儿子。
verses.en: But if he gives a gift from his inheritance to one of his servants, it will be his until the year of liberty;[NOTE:1] then it will revert to the prince. His inheritance will only remain with his sons.
notes: That is, the Year of Jubilee (Lev 25:8-15).
verses.commentary:
46:17 "the year of liberty" This refers to the "year of Jubilee" (cf. Lev. 25:8-17, esp. Ezek. 46:10), in
which the land returns to its original tribal owners because the land was a gift from YHWH (cf. Joshua 13-23).

Special Topic: Feasts of Israel, II. C.

verses.zh: 王不可夺取民的产业，以致驱逐他们离开所承受的；他要从自己的地业中，将产业赐给他儿子，免得我的民分散，各人离开所承受的。」
verses.en: The prince will not take away any of the people’s inheritance by oppressively removing them from their property. He will give his sons an inheritance from his own possessions so that my people will not be scattered, each from his own property.’”
verses.commentary:
46:18 This verse links to Ezek. 45:8, where the prince is given a large section of land to keep him from
taking common land from the people.

This shows that "the prince" was understood as a person still affected by Genesis 3. This would
not fit a NT understanding of "Messiah" (this is also true of Isa. 42:1 vs. 42:18-19). Oppression was often
associated with the kingship (cf. Ezek. 18:7,12,16).

verses.zh: 那带我的，将我从门旁进入之处、领进为祭司预备的圣屋，是朝北的，见后头西边有一块地。
verses.en: Then he brought me through the entrance, which was at the side of the gate, into the holy chambers for the priests, which faced north. There I saw[NOTE:1] a place at the extreme western end.
notes: The word הִנֵּה (hinneh, traditionally “behold”) indicates becoming aware of something and has been translated here as a verb.
verses.commentary:
46:19-20 This refers to the place where the priests prepared

- items to be offered

- items for them to eat

This food was holy and had to be prepared and eaten in a special holy place (cf. Ezek. 35:11-13)

verses.zh: 他对我说：「这是祭司煮赎愆祭、赎罪祭，烤素祭之地，免得带到外院，使民成圣。」
verses.en: He said to me, “This is the place where the priests will boil the guilt offering and the sin offering and where they will bake the grain offering, so that they do not bring them out to the outer court to transmit holiness to the people.”
verses.commentary: 46:20 See the same emphasis in Ezek. 44:19.

verses.zh: 他又带我到外院，使我经过院子的四拐角，见每拐角各有一个院子。
verses.en: Then he brought me out to the outer court and led me past the four corners of the court, and I noticed[NOTE:1] that in every corner of the court there was another court.
notes: The word הִנֵּה (hinneh, traditionally “behold”) indicates becoming aware of something and has been translated here as a verb.

verses.zh: 院子四拐角的院子，周围有墙，每院长四十肘，宽三十肘。四拐角院子的尺寸都是一样，
verses.en: In the four corners of the court were small[NOTE:1] courts, 70 feet[NOTE:2] in length and 52½ feet[NOTE:3] in width; the four were all the same size.
notes: The meaning of the Hebrew term is unclear. The LXX and Syriac render: “small.”
Heb “40 cubits” (i.e., 21 meters).
Heb “30 cubits” (i.e., 15.75 meters).
verses.commentary:
46:22 "corners. . .enclosed" Both of these words are uncertain.

- "corners" ‒ the VERB (BDB 893) is found only here in the OT. Many OT scholars assume it is a
Hophal PARTICIPLE. The NOUN is found in Ezek. 26:24; 36:29; 46:21 (twice). It could
refer to a corner post. Many of Ezekiel's architectural terms are rare and uncertain.

- "enclosed" ‒ BDB 883 (קטר) could also mean "vaulted" or "covered" (NEB, REB). JPSOA has
"uncovered" or "unroofed," following the Mishnah (Middoth 2.5). The Septuagint assumes a different stem
(קטנות), "smaller" (BDB 881-882), and is followed by Peshitta, NRSV, TEV, and NJB or possibly "the same size" (NEB, JPSOA footnote. REB).

verses.zh: 其中周围有一排房子，房子内有煮肉的地方。
verses.en: There was a row of masonry around each of the four courts, and places for boiling offerings were made under the rows all around.

verses.zh: 他对我说：「这都是煮肉的房子，殿内的仆役要在这里煮民的祭物。」
verses.en: Then he said to me, “These are the houses for boiling, where the ministers of the temple boil the sacrifices of the people.”

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible.
Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare your subject divisions with the five translations above. Paragraphing
is not inspired, but it is the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every paragraph has one and only one subject.

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: EZEKIEL 46:1-10

1'Thus says the Lord God, "The gate of the inner court facing east
shall be shut the six working days; but it shall be opened on the sabbath day and opened on the day of the new moon. 2The prince shall enter by way
of the porch of the gate from outside and stand by the post of the gate. Then the priests shall provide his burnt offering and his peace offerings, and he shall worship
at the threshold of the gate and then go out; but the gate shall not be shut until the evening. 3The people of the land shall also worship at the doorway
of that gate before the Lord on the sabbaths and on the new moons. 4The burnt offering which the prince shall offer to the
Lord on the sabbath day shall be six lambs without blemish and a ram without blemish; 5and the grain offering shall be an
ephah with the ram, and the grain offering with the lambs as much as he is able to give, and a hin of oil with an ephah. 6On the day of the new moon he
shall offer a young bull without blemish, also six lambs and a ram, which shall be without blemish. 7And he shall provide a grain offering, an ephah with
the bull and an ephah with the ram, and with the lambs as much as he is able, and a hin of oil with an ephah. 8When the prince enters, he shall go in by way
of the porch of the gate and go out by the same way. 9But when the people of the land come before the Lord at the appointed
feasts, he who enters by way of the north gate to worship shall go out by way of the south gate. And he who enters by way of the south gate shall go out by way of the north
gate. No one shall return by way of the gate by which he entered but shall go straight out. 10When they go in, the prince shall go in among them; and when
they go out, he shall go out."
